column1: legislative history
# 🆕 🔴 THE FINDING ACTION ND DID NOT ASK FOR, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES A PITCH:
# Article 5(1)(f) PROHIBITS AI systems inferring emotions from biometric data in EDUCATION
# INSTITUTIONS. It has applied since 2 FEBRUARY 2025. The Omnibus delayed HIGH-RISK
# obligations; it did NOT delay PROHIBITIONS. Penalty ceiling for an Article 5 breach:
# EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher — the Act's maximum.
#   -> So an EU education client's engagement/attention-analytics pilot sits on a LIVE
#      prohibition carrying the Act's heaviest penalty, more than two years BEFORE the
#      high-risk regime it is usually discussed under even begins.
#   -> 🟢 THE LINE THAT IS NOT CAUGHT: behavioural engagement analytics that do NOT infer
#      emotions fall outside Art. 5(1)(f). The prohibition is about INFERRING EMOTION from
#      BIOMETRIC data, not about analytics. That distinction is the deliverable.
#   -> 🔴 PROCTORING IS AN EXPLICIT GREY AREA: the Commission's guidelines leave open whether
#      a system with emotion inference as a SECONDARY functionality is caught. This KB
#      carries proctoring rows (api-evangelist/proctorio, shaheeranser/exam-proctor, the
#      seb-proctoring-validator and proctoring-reach-audit patterns). 🔵 Every one of them
#      now needs the question "does it infer emotion at all, even incidentally?" asked
#      before it is recommended into an EU engagement.
#   -> exception: medical or safety purposes.
# Source class: secondary (FPF blog, Commission FAQ via search result text, compliance
# commentary). The Commission's own FAQ host was BLOCKED.
# 🆕 🟢 TWO FURTHER EU EDUCATION INSTRUMENTS, both new to this KB, both secondary-sourced:
#   Council of the EU, ST-8262-2026-INIT, 24 April 2026 — calls for a coherent European
#     approach to AI in education: digital skills, AI literacy, teacher development,
#     critical thinking, and 🟢 an UPDATE OF THE DigCompEdu FRAMEWORK to cover educators'
#     AI use. 🔵 DigCompEdu is the competence frame EU public-sector education procurement
#     is written against, so an update to it is a procurement signal, not a policy opinion.
#   European Commission AI Literacy Framework for schools — learner expectations, learning
#     scenarios, classroom examples. Voluntary.
#   European Commission / Eurydice, "Digital education at school in Europe 2026: Bridging
#     gaps in access, teaching and learning" — infrastructure, student competences, teacher
#     preparation.
#   🔴 All three hosts blocked; titles and content relayed through search results only.
